about: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (official FP8 / MXFP4 checkpoint, unchanged) on 4x H200 NVL, TP4, 262K, 256 sequences, DSpark k=5: vLLM main 51d2a855 + vllm#64893 (latency_specialized decode executor for Hopper TP4) + lossless Hopper patches (P2P-store fallback for the executor's all-reduce on NVLink-bridged H200 NVL without NVSwitch, exact BF16 dense operands, hybrid adaptive verification above 16 requests, MXFP4 Marlin padding 576, small-head sparse decode) + Engram tables read from the checkpoint on NVMe. Image: sybil-solutions/local-ai-images vllm-dsv41-h200.
setup: Download deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 at the pinned revision (510 GB) to local NVMe and mount it at /models. The image reads the Engram tables from that directory at every decode step (DSV41_ENGRAM_DISK=1 in the image ENV), so keep it on NVMe, not network storage. The first start JIT-compiles FlashInfer and CuTe kernels for several minutes; mount /root/.cache to keep them. Clients should ask for usage once at the end (stream_options include_usage, the OpenAI default): with a reasoning parser, continuous_usage_stats makes vLLM recount the reasoning tokens of the whole output on every chunk, which cut 8k decode at 160 users from 6,810 to 1,290 tok/s here.
